metaDescription: Compare Rize-Artvin (RZV) and Trabzon (TZX) airports for Ayder, Pokut, and Sümela. Domestic hiking gear rules and 4x4 rental advice for 2026.
quickAnswer: Choosing between Istanbul to Trabzon (TZX) and Rize-Artvin (RZV) flights depends on your primary base. Fly into RZV for Ayder, Pokut, Çamlıhemşin, and Artvin, saving up to two hours of coastal driving. Choose TZX if Sümela Monastery, Uzungöl, or higher daily flight frequency from Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) matter most.

body.text: When should you fly into Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV) instead of Trabzon (TZX)?

Fly into Rize-Artvin Airport (RZV) whenever your itinerary centres on the Fırtına Valley, Ayder Plateau, Pokut, Çamlıhemşin, Borçka Karagöl, or macahel trekking routes. Built on reclaimed sea land between Pazar and Yeşilköy, RZV places you directly in the eastern Kaçkar foothills, cutting roughly 90 to 120 minutes off each coastal drive compared with landing at Trabzon.

Trabzon Airport (TZX) remains the stronger hub when you need flexible departure waves or plan to visit Sümela Monastery and Uzungöl first. According to [DHMİ flight operations](https://dhmi.gov.tr/sayfalar/tumucuslar.aspx), TZX handles significantly more daily rotations from both IST and SAW, with Turkish Airlines, [Pegasus Airlines](https://www.flypgs.com/en/express-baggage), and [AJet](https://ajet.com/en/discover/campaigns/exclusive-check-in-baggage-allowance-for-flex-and-premium-packages-2) competing across morning, midday, and late-evening slots. DHMİ has also broken ground on the [Trabzon New Airport project](https://dhmi.gov.tr/Sayfalar/Haber/trabzon-yeni-havalimaninda-santiye-calismalari-basladi.aspx), though the existing terminal serves all 2026 traffic.

An open-jaw routing—flying into TZX and departing from RZV, or vice versa—often works best for seven-day Black Sea trips. You visit Sümela Monastery on day one, move east through tea-growing valleys, and fly back to Istanbul from RZV without backtracking along the D010 coastal highway.
How far are RZV and TZX from Ayder, Pokut and Sümela?

Driving times across the eastern Black Sea depend on mountain switchbacks, summer mist, and roadworks rather than straight-line distance. From Rize-Artvin (RZV), Ayder Plateau is roughly 52 km (1 hour 10 minutes), while Pokut Plateau requires 55 km and at least 2 hours due to the steep unpaved climb. From Trabzon (TZX), Sümela Monastery is just 46 km (1 hour).

body.text: How do baggage rules apply to hiking gear on domestic flights?

On Istanbul to Trabzon and Rize flights, standard domestic economy fares include 15 kg of checked baggage on Turkish Airlines and tiered allowances on Pegasus and AJet. Trekking poles, tent pegs, and multi-tools are strictly prohibited in cabin luggage and must travel inside checked bags, while oversized mountaineering packs trigger special sports-equipment or excess-weight charges.
Check carrier rules before booking low-cost domestic tickets:

items: Trekking poles and metal pegs: Pack collapsed poles inside your checked duffel; airport security at IST and SAW confiscates poles at cabin X-ray.

Turkish Airlines sports gear: Under [Turkish Airlines sports equipment rules](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/sports-equipment/), dedicated sports sets are accepted only as checked baggage up to 23 kg and should be declared during reservation.

Pegasus Airlines bundles: Review the [Pegasus baggage allowance](https://www.flypgs.com/en/pegasus-baggage-allowance) and [special services price table](https://www.flypgs.com/en/useful-info/other-info/extra-services-price-table) before checkout; adding extra kilos online costs far less than paying at the counter.

AJet sports equipment: Per [AJet baggage conditions](https://ajet.com/en/corporate/rules-and-conditions/baggage), declared sports equipment falls outside free baggage allowances and incurs a route-specific tariff.
Camp stoves and fuel: Gas canisters are banned in both cabin and checked luggage; buy screw-on butane canisters locally in Trabzon or Rize.

body.text: Can you rent a 4x4 directly at the terminal?

Yes, major national and international car-rental desks operate inside both Trabzon (TZX) and Rize-Artvin (RZV) arrival halls, but genuine 4x4 inventory is limited—especially between June and September. You must reserve a high-clearance AWD or 4WD SUV weeks ahead and verify in writing that the contract permits driving on unpaved highland (yayla) tracks.

Standard rental policies in Türkiye frequently exclude tyre, underbody, and windscreen damage on non-asphalt roads. For Pokut, Gito, or Elevit plateaus, many independent travellers rent a standard sedan or compact crossover for coastal towns and hire a local highland driver with a licensed 4x4 minibus in Çamlıhemşin for the steep dirt ascents.

faq.q: How long is the flight from Istanbul to Trabzon or Rize-Artvin?
faq.a: Direct flights from Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) to Trabzon (TZX) take approximately 1 hour 45 minutes. Flights to Rize-Artvin (RZV) take roughly 1 hour 55 minutes depending on seasonal Black Sea winds.

faq.q: Do both IST and SAW have direct flights to Rize-Artvin (RZV)?
faq.a: Yes. Turkish Airlines operates direct flights from IST to RZV, while AJet and Pegasus serve RZV from SAW. Check seasonal schedules early during winter months when frequencies decrease.

faq.q: Is fog a major delay risk at Trabzon and Rize-Artvin airports?
faq.a: Low coastal cloud and spring fog can occasionally delay morning landings along the eastern Black Sea. Leave at least four to five hours before any separate international departure in Istanbul.

faq.q: Are Havaş airport shuttles available from RZV to Rize and Hopa?
faq.a: Yes. Scheduled airport coaches connect Rize-Artvin Airport west toward Rize city centre and east toward Ardeşen, Pazar, Fındıklı, Arhavi, and Hopa after domestic arrivals.

faq.q: Should I drive myself to Pokut Plateau in a rental car?
faq.a: Only if you have a genuine high-clearance 4x4, mountain driving experience, and clear dry weather. After rain, the clay-and-stone road above Şenyuva becomes slippery and narrow, making a local driver safer.

faq.q: Can I bring hiking boots and a daypack in the cabin?
faq.a: Yes. Clean hiking boots and a daypack within your airline's cabin dimensions (typically 55x40x23 cm on domestic flights) are permitted, provided all sharp tools, knives, and poles are checked.
